newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp steel workers end week-long strike.
newsitem.headline: Krupp steel workers end week-long strike.

text.p: Workers at Krupp AG steel mills returned to work on Friday morning after receiving guarantees that the planned joint venture between Krupp and Thyssen AG would not bring immediate forced job cuts.
An official at Krupp's Dortmund plant confirmed that work had resumed after a week of interruption as details of the controversial merger were agreed.
Krupp's workers' council said late on Thursday that work would resume at plants in Dortmund, Bochum and Siegerland as of the early shift on Friday.

The decision came in response to a written guarantee from Krupp and Thyssen that no forced job cuts would occur before December 31 2000 and that trainee numbers would be maintained, Krupp's works council said.
Separately, the powerful IG Metall engineering union added that it had secured agreement that 600 extra jobs would be created in Dortmund as a result of the merger.
After an abortive hostile takeover bid by Krupp, Krupp and Thyssen this week agreed to merge their steel activities into a joint venture as of April 1, creating Europe's largest steel company.
The plans triggered mass protests from workers fearing as many as 8,000 job cuts.

Thyssen chairman Dieter Vogel, speaking on Thursday after Thyssen's supervisory board gave unanimous approval to the deal, said the number of job losses resulting from the merger would be lower than announced by the two sides when they signed a memorandum of understanding on Wednesday.
From a workforce of 23,600 at the start of 1997, 6,600 jobs would be shed by the year 2001, he said.
Vogel also said the Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp group would bear all the restructuring costs from the venture of which Thyssen will own 60 percent and Krupp 40 percent.
Thyssen Krupp Stahl will have sales of 11 billion marks and output of 15 million tonnes a year.
Krupp's supervisory board is due to review the deal on April 2, and chief executive Gerhard Cromme is to hold a news conference on Friday morning in Essen.
